articles.title: Dark Matter That Bumps Into Itself Could Crack Three Cosmic Cold Cases
articles.summary: A new theory proposes that dark matter particles can collide, unlike the standard 'ghostly' model. This self-interaction could explain an ultradense clump, a scarred star stream, and a mysteriously dense star cluster. The same mechanism works across vastly different scales, from distant galaxies to our own neighborhood.

articles.title: Injectable Biomaterial Travels Through Bloodstream to Mend Hearts from Within
articles.summary: A nano-sized biomaterial derived from heart tissue can be infused into blood vessels after a heart attack. In animal studies, it bound to leaky vessels, reduced inflammation, and improved cardiac function. The approach could one day treat traumatic brain injury and pulmonary hypertension without invasive surgery.

articles.title: Hidden in a Retaining Wall for Decades: 240-Million-Year-Old Giant Amphibian Finally Named
articles.summary: A fossil discovered by a retired chicken farmer in a quarry rock used for a garden wall has been identified as Arenaerpeton, a 1.2-meter-long temnospondyl. The specimen preserves rare soft tissue outlines and a full articulated skeleton, making it one of Australia's most significant fossil finds in decades.
